title: Khubz (Arabic Flatbread)
description: Khubz is a traditional Arabic flatbread known for its soft, airy texture and signature pocket. It is commonly served fresh with mezze, used for scooping dips, or filled with grilled meats and vegetables.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: 500 g (4 cups) strong bread flour (high-protein, for elasticity)
10 g (1 tbsp) olive oil (plus more for brushing)
7 g (1 packet) instant yeast (or 20 g fresh yeast)

instruction.title: Method
steps:
1. Dough Preparation:
• In a large mixing bowl (or stand mixer), combine warm water, sugar, and yeast. Let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
• Add flour and salt gradually, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
• Knead (10 min by hand or 6 min with dough hook) until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky.
• Add olive oil during kneading to develop a silky dough.

2. First Rise:
• Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise 1–1.5 hours until doubled in size.

3. Shaping:
• Punch down gently.
• Divide into 8 equal balls (~100 g each).
• Cover with a cloth and let rest 15 min.
• Roll each ball into a flat round (20 cm / 8-inch, about 5 mm thick). Keep covered to prevent drying.

4. Baking (Restaurant Technique):
• Option A – Oven: Preheat oven to 250°C / 480°F with a pizza stone or heavy baking steel inside. Place 2–3 rounds directly on the hot stone. Bake 2–3 minutes until puffed and lightly golden.
• Option B – Cast Iron Pan: Heat pan over high heat until very hot. Cook 1–2 minutes per side, pressing gently to encourage puffing.

5. Finishing:
• Keep baked Khubz wrapped in a clean towel to retain softness.
• Brush lightly with olive oil for sheen (optional).

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with hummus, baba ghanoush, and labneh.
Use for wraps with grilled meats or vegetables.
Enjoy fresh with olive oil and za’atar.

chefTips: Puffing (Pocket Effect) requires very high heat and evenly rolled dough.
Keep dough thickness uniform for consistent pocket formation.
Do not over-flour while rolling to maintain proper puffing.
Best served fresh; reheat in a hot oven for 1–2 minutes if needed.
